statement: Never `git add -A`, `git add .`, or `git commit -a` in this repo; stage by explicit path and commit with `git commit --only <paths>`
rationale: Multiple Claude Code sessions share one working tree on main. The .git/index is a single shared file — a broad add/commit sweeps in a sibling session's uncommitted, unrelated edits into your commit. Observed directly: a `git commit --only static/app.js static/app.css static/index.html` still produced 1174 insertions/122 deletions (far more than the actual diff) because a sibling session had an in-progress queue-panel redesign uncommitted in the same three files — --only operates on working-tree state per path, not "my hunks," so it doesn't isolate sibling edits within a shared file either. Remediation when it already happened: amend the message to honestly describe the mixed content, never surgically extract (risks losing the sibling's work).
